title: kubestream — Flap Report
description: Objects that will not hold still. Ranks every watched object by how many Modified rows it produced in the selected window and compares that against a threshold you set, so 'this controller is fighting another one' becomes a number instead of a hunch. Flapping is expensive twice over — it burns apiserver and it fills this table — so the objects at the top are usually both a correctness bug and a cost line.

list.name: datasource
list.label: Data source
list.description: The ClickHouse holding kubestream's resource_states table.

list.name: cluster
list.label: Cluster
list.description: cluster_id is the leading column of the sort key, so every panel filters on it.
list.definition: SELECT DISTINCT cluster_id FROM resource_states ORDER BY cluster_id

query.rawSql: SELECT DISTINCT cluster_id FROM resource_states ORDER BY cluster_id

list.name: namespace
list.label: Namespace
list.description: Multi-select, All by default. Flapping is often confined to one namespace's operator, so narrowing here is the first bisect.
list.definition: SELECT DISTINCT namespace FROM resource_states WHERE cluster_id = ${cluster:sqlstring} ORDER BY namespace

query.rawSql: SELECT DISTINCT namespace FROM resource_states WHERE cluster_id = ${cluster:sqlstring} ORDER BY namespace

list.name: kind
list.label: Kind
list.description: Multi-select, All by default. Status-heavy kinds flap by nature; excluding them is how the list becomes actionable.
list.definition: SELECT DISTINCT kind FROM resource_states WHERE cluster_id = ${cluster:sqlstring} ORDER BY kind

query.rawSql: SELECT DISTINCT kind FROM resource_states WHERE cluster_id = ${cluster:sqlstring} ORDER BY kind

list.name: threshold
list.label: Flap threshold (changes per window)
list.description: How many Modified rows in the dashboard's time range make an object a flapper. It is a plain number, and it is read by the SQL rather than by a panel setting — Grafana cannot interpolate a variable into a panel's threshold configuration, so the threshold line on the timeline is a series the query returns rather than a static line that would silently disagree with this box.

panels.title: Objects over the flap threshold
panels.description: How many distinct objects exceeded the threshold in this window. Zero is the healthy reading. Watch this after changing a controller: a fix that stops a fight shows up here within one window, long before it is visible in the ranking table.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT count() AS objects_over_threshold
FROM
(
    SELECT namespace, kind, name
    FROM resource_states FINAL
    WHERE cluster_id = ${cluster:sqlstring}
      AND namespace IN (${namespace:sqlstring})
      AND kind IN (${kind:sqlstring})
      AND event_type IN ('Modified', 'Checkpoint')
      AND $__timeFilter(ts)
    GROUP BY namespace, kind, name
    HAVING count() >= ${threshold}
)

panels.title: Modified rows in window
panels.description: Total change volume behind the ranking, for scale. A high flapper count against a low total means a few objects churning in an otherwise quiet cluster; a high total means the whole cluster is moving and the threshold probably needs raising for this window length.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT count() AS modified_rows
FROM resource_states FINAL
WHERE cluster_id = ${cluster:sqlstring}
  AND namespace IN (${namespace:sqlstring})
  AND kind IN (${kind:sqlstring})
  AND event_type IN ('Modified', 'Checkpoint')
  AND $__timeFilter(ts)

panels.title: Flapping objects over time, against the threshold
panels.description: One series per object that cleared the threshold over the whole window, bucketed to the dashboard interval, plus a dashed threshold line. Query B exists only to draw that line: it returns the threshold variable as a constant series, because a panel-level threshold cannot read a dashboard variable and a hard-coded one would drift away from the box above. Series that cross the line in bursts are fights; series that sit on it are steady-state churn.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
    $__timeInterval(ts) AS time,
    concat(namespace, '/', kind, '/', name) AS object,
    count() AS modifications
FROM resource_states FINAL
WHERE cluster_id = ${cluster:sqlstring}
  AND namespace IN (${namespace:sqlstring})
  AND kind IN (${kind:sqlstring})
  AND event_type IN ('Modified', 'Checkpoint')
  AND $__timeFilter(ts)
  AND (namespace, kind, name) IN
  (
      SELECT namespace, kind, name
      FROM resource_states FINAL
      WHERE cluster_id = ${cluster:sqlstring}
        AND namespace IN (${namespace:sqlstring})
        AND kind IN (${kind:sqlstring})
        AND event_type IN ('Modified', 'Checkpoint')
        AND $__timeFilter(ts)
      GROUP BY namespace, kind, name
      HAVING count() >= ${threshold}
  )
GROUP BY time, object
ORDER BY time

SELECT
    $__timeInterval(ts) AS time,
    toUInt32(${threshold}) AS threshold
FROM resource_states
WHERE cluster_id = ${cluster:sqlstring}
  AND $__timeFilter(ts)
GROUP BY time
ORDER BY time

panels.title: Objects by change count
panels.description: The ranking, threshold included as a column so a row can be read against it without leaving the table. field_managers is the union of every field manager seen on those rows — two or more controller names on a high-count row is the signature of a fight, where one name repeated is usually a controller re-reconciling its own status. Take namespace, kind and name to the Object Timeline dashboard to read the individual diffs.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
    namespace,
    kind,
    name,
    count()                AS modifications,
    toUInt32(${threshold}) AS threshold,
    max(ts)                AS last_change,
    arrayStringConcat(arraySort(groupUniqArrayArray(actors)), ', ') AS field_managers
FROM resource_states FINAL
WHERE cluster_id = ${cluster:sqlstring}
  AND namespace IN (${namespace:sqlstring})
  AND kind IN (${kind:sqlstring})
  AND event_type IN ('Modified', 'Checkpoint')
  AND $__timeFilter(ts)
GROUP BY namespace, kind, name
ORDER BY modifications DESC
LIMIT 100
